{{Quote|I will watch your struggles and remember them for all time.|[[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], to Bidlo Kwerve|translated=1|<ref name="rancor" />}}
'''Bidlo Kwerve''' was a [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] who served [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. A tall, grizzled [[Gender/Legends|man]] with scarred features and a mane of black hair, he was known for his greediness and hot temper, and was quick to respond to any perceived insults. Kwerve and a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] named [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] competed to become Jabba's new [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]] after the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] deemed his previous retainer, [[Naroon Cuthus]], too old and incapable of carrying out his duties. Kwerve and Fortuna hated each other with a passion and went to great lengths to prove themselves in Jabba's eyes, though Jabba considered each as incompetent as the other.

Kwerve disliked Jabba's top [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], and the two often clashed, both in words and with [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]]. Around [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], he considered leaving Jabba's employ because of the continual menial tasks that were being asked of him, and though Fortuna encouraged him to quit, he never did. Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Kwerve discovered a crashed [[Starship/Legends|ship]] in the [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooinian]] desert, with a live [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|rancor]] inside it. Hoping to present the beast to Jabba for his birthday, he begrudgingly sought the aid of Fortuna to help him transport it to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. Jabba was impressed with the initiative shown by his two top lieutenants and offered to make one of them his new majordomo; the other would be given the "greater honor," though Jabba did not specify what this was. Ever greedy, Kwerve accepted the "greater honor"&mdash;he became the rancor's first victim and was killed in a pit below Jabba's court. The uncouth Corellian did get his revenge, posthumously, when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] used Kwerve's skull to kill the rancor in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].

==Biography==
===Jabba's lieutenant===
{{Quote|Oh, and as a bonus&hellip; I won't lecture you on hiring from the wrong end of the food chain.|Han Solo speaking about Bidlo Kwerve, to Jabba Desilijic Tiure|<ref name="crumb" />}}
[[File:JabbaHookah-ROTJ.png|left|thumb|250x250px|[[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], Kwerse's boss.]]
Bidlo Kwerve, an uncouth [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] from [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], found himself in a life of crime, becoming a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]]<ref name="gg5" /> and a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]].<ref name="EGTC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Known as something of a ruffian,<ref name="rebel dawn">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> and always quick to brandish his [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]], Kwerve had an unkempt mane of black hair, with a thin white stripe running from front to back,<ref name="crumb" /> and a craggy, scarred face. At some point in his life, Kwerve began to work for [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], becoming one of his top lieutenants.<ref name="rebel dawn" />

Kwerve sought to replace [[Naroon Cuthus]], Jabba's aging and increasingly inept [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]], but he had stiff competition in the form of [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]], a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Slavery/Legends|slaver]] who had once held the prestigious position decades earlier, but had been demoted for some frivolous error.<ref name="NEGTC" /> It amused Jabba to watch the two fight it out, and he constantly pitted them against each other, knowing that one would eventually triumph over the other and replace the bumbling Naroon Cuthus. The two hated each other to a fault,<ref name="gg5" /> though Kwerve was almost universally disliked anyway.<ref name="rebel dawn" /> The Corellian pirate's duties varied considerably; he often acted as a [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]] for Jabba, helped perform menial tasks such as stocking [[Starship/Legends|ships]],<ref name="crumb" /> administered [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|Jabba's townhouse]] in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] while the Hutt was elsewhere,<ref name="gg7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref> and accepted incoming calls to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] and referred them to the Hutt.<ref name="rebel dawn" /> In the race to prove themselves in Jabba's eyes, Fortuna edged ahead; the Twi'lek had better administration and management skills,<ref name="EGTC" /> he fawned over Jabba more than his opponent,<ref name="mts">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> and he could speak and understand [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], unlike Kwerve.<ref name="rancor" />

===Competition===
{{Quote|Master, I shall be satisfied with the majordomo position. As Bidlo Kwerve has pointed out, he performed the greatest service to you. Please allow him to have the greater honor.|translated=1|Bib Fortuna, to Jabba the Hutt|<ref name="rancor" />}}
As Jabba grew weary of the aging Cuthus, the rivalry between Kwerve and Fortuna heated up.<ref name="NEGTC" /> In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], Kwerve and Fortuna accompanied Jabba to [[Kwenn Space Station/Legends|Space Station Kwenn]] to meet with his top pilot, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], and collect a recently smuggled load of [[Spice/Legends|spice]]. Jabba and Solo had agreed to meet alone, but the Hutt decided to bring his two henchmen anyway; furious, Solo insulted them, and Kwerve had to be restrained by Jabba from attacking him. When Solo insulted him again, Kwerve pulled a blaster on him, though the pilot's hidden [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] companion, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], destroyed the weapon with his [[Bowcaster/Legends|bowcaster]]. Solo departed before things escalated, though Kwerve attempted to persuade his master to [[Death/Legends|kill]] the Corellian pilot and his Wookiee first mate.<ref name="crumb" />

[[File:Kwerve_shooting.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Kwerve and Fortuna, attempting to catch Salacious Crumb.]]Jabba ordered his two lieutenants to stock his ship with the spice; furious at having to perform such menial duties, Kwerve began wondering how much more of Jabba's abuse he could take. He voiced his annoyance to Fortuna, but the Twi'lek merely encouraged him to leave. Later, en route to Jabba's residence on Tatooine, the Hutt remonstrated with his two lieutenants, berating them for not noticing Chewbacca before his appearance. Jabba dismissed the duo, telling them he would contemplate their punishment over dinner,<ref name="crumb" /> and the two left to continue arguing.<ref name="EGTC" /> During Jabba's meal, however, they heard a disturbance and entered to find the Hutt struggling to capture a small [[Kowakian monkey-lizard/Legends|Kowakian monkey-lizard]]. Jabba had found the creature in his food bowl, and Kwerve drew his blaster, hoping to kill it. [[Salacious B. Crumb/Legends|Salacious B. Crumb]], as the creature was called, covered Kwerve and Fortuna in Jabba's [[Higartha brain-stew|goo-like food]] before Kwerve could pull the trigger, rendering the blaster nonfunctional. Jabba was so amused by these events that he sent his two lieutenants away, ultimately hiring Crumb as a court jester.<ref name="crumb" />

[[0 BBY/Legends|Two years later]], Kwerve was temporarily appointed as Jabba's majordomo. During this time, he again clashed with Han Solo, after the pilot had dropped a load of valuable spice during an Imperial search. Solo had contacted Jabba's Palace to reason with the Hutt, though Kwerve was first to answer the call; he eventually put Solo through to Jabba, after much gloating.<ref name="rebel dawn" /> After this, however, his temporary promotion was rescinded. A few days later, Kwerve was presented with an opportunity to edge ahead of Fortuna in the contest to become his master's new majordomo.<ref name="rancor" />

A group of [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] informed Kwerve that a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] ship had crashed in the Tatooinian desert, containing a [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|fearsome creature]],<ref name="SWTS:SE">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref> and persuaded him to buy the wreckage from them.<ref name="wotc">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/Rancor2|series=Jabba's Rancor|text=Part 2: The Birthday Present}}</ref> Intrigued, and hoping to curry favor with Jabba, Kwerve went out to investigate along with several of Jabba's [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] guards,<ref name="db">{{DB|creature|rancor|rancor}}</ref> claiming he was going [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]] hunting.<ref name="wotc" /> However, Bib Fortuna&mdash;always keeping tabs on his rival&mdash;was not far behind him.<ref name="gg5" /> In the downed ship, Bidlo Kwerve found a hulking, meters-tall beast, which was only subdued when the Corellian pirate threw eight [[Gas grenade/Legends|gas grenades]] at it.<ref name="rancor" /> Fortuna arrived on the scene moments later, demanding to know what was going on.<ref name="db" /> Both he and Kwerve knew they would not be able to bring the beast back to Jabba's Palace alone and decided that working together&mdash;something they had never done before&mdash;was the least dangerous option.<ref name="gg5" /> The duo took the creature to the lower dungeons of the desert citadel, and Fortuna used his contacts to secure the services of [[Malakili/Legends|Malakili]], a beast handler at [[Circus Horrificus/Legends|Circus Horrificus]].<ref name="rancor" />

===Death===
During this time, Jabba was away on business purchasing a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] in Mos Eisley; his birthday was in three days, and Fortuna and Malakili hoped to present the creature to him as a gift. Malakili, freshly arrived from [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], identified the creature as a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]], a [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]], though how the rancor ended up on Tatooine eluded him. Kwerve and Fortuna installed a trapdoor in front of Jabba's dais, so that the Hutt could pull a lever and those standing over the grating would fall into a special dungeon containing the rancor. Although Jabba's [[Spy/Legends|spies]] around the palace had informed him of the newly arrived rancor before his birthday, he was genuinely pleased to see the creature; Kwerve took this opportunity to claim most of the credit for the beast's capture, though Fortuna told Jabba of the administrative duties he had performed. Impressed at the initiative shown by the two beings, Jabba promised to make one of them his new majordomo, while the other would get a greater, unspecified role that would be remembered forever.<ref name="rancor" />
[[File:Rancor-RotJAVA.png|left|thumb|250x250px|The Rancor gifted to Jabba ended up eating Kwerve.]]
Fortuna, ever cagey, noted the sinister nature of Jabba's latter promise and voiced his contentedness at accepting the lesser honor of becoming the majordomo. Kwerve was satisfied and waited for his great honor; Jabba and Fortuna spoke in Huttese, and as Kwerve could not understand he began to panic. Eventually, Jabba revealed what the great honor would be: Kwerve would be the first victim of the rancor. The trapdoor opened, and Bidlo Kwerve was devoured by the rancor, despite fighting back with his holdout blaster.<ref name="rancor" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Let's see&hellip; ahh. The skull of a previous dinner guest. This oughta do it.|Luke Skywalker, moments before using Kwerve's skull to trigger the blast door that killed the rancor|<ref name="Return of the Jedi: The National Public Radio Dramatization">[[Return of the Jedi: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''Return of the Jedi'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref>}}
[[File:Kwerve_skull.jpg|thumb|220px|Bidlo Kwerve's skull, moments before the rancor's death]]
For four years<ref>''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' places Kwerve's death in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] while [[The Essential Atlas|''The Essential Atlas'']] places the [[Siege of Jabba's Palace]] (including the Rancor's death) in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].</ref> Kweve's remains continued to stay in the Rancor's pit and eventually only his bones were found.<ref name=":0" /> Ironically, he would get his revenge&mdash;albeit posthumously&mdash;on the rancor<ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Skull}}</ref> when [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] used<ref name=":0" /> Kwerve's<ref name="ccg" /> skull to trigger the closing mechanism of a [[Blast door/Legends|blast door]] in the dungeon, killing the rancor.<ref name=":0">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Upon finding the skull, he described it as the skull of a "previous dinner guest".<ref name="Return of the Jedi: The National Public Radio Dramatization" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Maybe one of your girlfriends wants to dance?''"<br />"''That does it, Solo&mdash;!|Han Solo and Bidlo Kwerve on Space Station Kwenn|<ref name="crumb" />}}
[[File:Kwerve_angry.jpg|thumb|170px|Bidlo Kwerve|left]]
Bidlo Kwerve was considered a thug, and he had a brash, aggressive nature. Insults against him rarely went unpunished, and he had a cruel sense of humor; he taunted Han Solo after the pilot had dropped his cargo and earned Jabba's wrath.<ref name="rebel dawn" /> Kwerve was thought to be extremely lucky, a trait many believed was shared by most Corellians, and this was one of the reasons Bib Fortuna loathed him so.<ref name="gg5" /> He rarely spoke; Malakili reckoned this was because he had a high, raspy, and whiny voice. Kwerve was thought to be very greedy, always looking out for himself; unlike Fortuna, he did not have the presence of mind to decline Jabba's offer of a "greater honor," instead claiming it for himself, ultimately to his own detriment. He was also an opportunist; when he heard about the downed ship in the desert, he traveled there personally to investigate, hoping to turn things to his advantage. His appearance reflected his uncouth nature, with wild, ragged black hair and a face pockmarked with numerous scars and sores, including one long scar from a blaster wound.<ref name="rancor" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Kwerve_BBE.jpg|thumb|270x270px|A non-canon depiction of Kwerve from ''Best Birthday Ever'']]
The character of Bidlo Kwerve first appeared in numerous [[West End Games]] sourcebooks, in biographies for Bib Fortuna,<ref name=":1">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> a minor character from [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name=":0" /> He first appeared in [[Bill Slavicsek]] and [[Curtis Smith]]'s ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'',<ref name=":1" /> but ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]'', written by [[Michael Stern]], expanded his backstory.<ref name="gg5" /> [[Kevin J. Anderson]] used this [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying-game information]] for part of his short story in ''[[Tales from Jabba's Palace]]'', "[[A Boy and His Monster: The Rancor Keeper's Tale]]," in [[1996]],<ref name="rancor" /> and in the same year, Kwerve was given his first visual appearance in [[Ryder Windham]]'s ''[[This Crumb for Hire]]''.<ref name="crumb" />

[[Decipher]]'s [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the skull used by Luke Skywalker to kill the rancor in ''Return of the Jedi'' as Kwerve's, tying in to his death<ref name="ccg" /> in ''Tales from Jabba's Palace''.<ref name="rancor" /> The character has since appeared briefly in [[A. C. Crispin]]'s ''[[Rebel Dawn]]''<ref name="rebel dawn" /> and the non-[[canon]] ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' comic "[[Best Birthday Ever]]," which tells the story of "A Boy and His Monster" in a more lighthearted way. In it, Kwerve lends his [[Landspeeder/Legends|speeder]] to Bib Fortuna to collect the rancor from the [[Interstellar Parcel Service/Legends|Interstellar Parcel Service]], but dies<ref name="Best Birthday Ever">{{Tales|16|Best Birthday Ever}}</ref> similarly to "A Boy and His Monster."<ref name="rancor" />

In the [[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 1|first issue of the manga adaptation]] of {{Film|VI}} Kwerve's skull is depicted as non-[[Human/Legends|human]], sporting sharp teeth and a wider jaw, which is shown still attached to the skull.<ref name="Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 1">[[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 1|''Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi'' 1]]</ref>
